subject: math
title: Multiplication Facts to 10 × 10
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplication Facts Worksheets: Times Tables to 10 × 10 with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Recall and demonstrate multiplication facts for 1 × 1 to 10 × 10, and related division facts
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on the multiplication facts to 10 × 10: arrays, strategies for the 6s, 7s, 8s and 9s, fact families, related division facts, missing factors and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Ontario curriculum.
key_big: Learn a strategy for each fact: double the 3s for the 6s, double the 4s for the 8s, and use the 10s for the 9s.
key_sub: Every fact gives division facts: 7 × 8 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Remember 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8.
body_html:
Know every fact to 10 × 10

In Grade 4 you learn all the multiplication facts from 1 × 1 to 10 × 10. 7 × 6 means 7 groups of 6. You can multiply in any order: 6 × 7 is the same as 7 × 6. So if you know the 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s and 10s, only a few facts are left to learn.

A strategy for each fact

FactsStrategyExample
× 2Double the number2 × 8: 8 + 8 = 16
× 3Double, then add one more group3 × 7: 14 + 7 = 21
× 4Double, then double again4 × 6: 12, 24
× 5Half of the 10s5 × 8: half of 80 = 40
× 6Double the 3s6 × 7: 21 + 21 = 42
× 75s + 2s7 × 8: 40 + 16 = 56
× 8Double the 4s8 × 6: 24 + 24 = 48
× 910s take away one group9 × 7: 70 − 7 = 63
× 10Count the tens10 × 6 = 60

The 9s finger trick. Hold up 10 fingers. For 9 × 4, fold down finger 4. The 3 fingers to the left are tens and the 6 to the right are ones: 36.

Near fact

7 × 7 = 49. What is 7 × 8?

7 × 8 is one more group of 7: 49 + 7 = 56.

Answer: 56

Every fact gives division facts

Division undoes multiplication. 6, 9 and 54 make a fact family: 6 × 9 = 54, 9 × 6 = 54, 54 ÷ 6 = 9 and 54 ÷ 9 = 6. A division fact starts with the biggest number.

Division

63 ÷ 9 = ?

Think: 9 × ? = 63. 9 × 7 = 63.

Answer: 7

Missing factor

? × 8 = 48

Think: 48 ÷ 8. 6 × 8 = 48.

Answer: 6

Word problem

Muffins come in trays of 6. How many muffins are in 8 trays?

8 groups of 6: 3 × 8 = 24, double 24 = 48. So 8 × 6 = 48.

Answer: 48 muffins

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up 7 × 8 = 54 and 6 × 9 = 54Say 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8
Adding instead of multiplying: 6 × 9 = 15× means groups of: 6 groups of 9 = 54
9s from 10s: 10 × 7 − 1 = 69Take away a whole group: 70 − 7 = 63
Turning division around: 8 ÷ 56 = 7Start with the biggest number: 56 ÷ 8 = 7

faq.q: What multiplication facts should a Grade 4 student know in Ontario?
faq.a: The Ontario Mathematics Curriculum (2020) asks Grade 4 students to recall the multiplication facts from 1 × 1 to 10 × 10 and the related division facts, such as 7 × 8 = 56 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7. In Grade 3 they learned the facts for 2, 5 and 10.

faq.q: Do Grade 4 students write EQAO in Ontario?
faq.a: No. Ontario students write the EQAO assessments in Grades 3 and 6. Knowing every fact to 10 × 10 in Grade 4 builds a strong base for Grade 5 and Grade 6 math.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to remember 7 × 8?
How can I help my child learn the 6, 7, 8 and 9 times tables?
faq.a: Teach one strategy for each: double the 3s for the 6s, double the 4s for the 8s, and use the 10s and take away one group for the 9s. Practise a few facts each day and ask for the related division fact too.

Skip count by 3s. What comes next?
12, 15, 18, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 18 + 3 = 21. So 3 × 7 = 21.

sets.title: Strategies for 6, 7, 8 and 9: doubles, the 9s trick and near facts

items.q: 3 × 7 = 21. Double it to find 6 × 7.
items.e: 6 is double 3, so 6 × 7 is double 3 × 7: 21 + 21 = 42.

items.q: 3 × 8 = 24. Double it to find 6 × 8.
items.e: 6 is double 3, so 6 × 8 is double 3 × 8: 24 + 24 = 48.

items.q: 3 × 9 = 27. Double it to find 6 × 9.
items.e: 6 is double 3, so 6 × 9 is double 3 × 9: 27 + 27 = 54.

items.q: 3 × 6 = 18. Double it to find 6 × 6.
items.e: 6 is double 3, so 6 × 6 is double 3 × 6: 18 + 18 = 36.

items.q: The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 4, fold down finger 4. What is 9 × 4?
items.e: Finger 4 is down. There are 3 fingers to the left (tens) and 6 to the right (ones), so 9 × 4 = 36. Read the left side first.

items.q: The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 7, fold down finger 7. What is 9 × 7?
items.e: Finger 7 is down. There are 6 fingers to the left (tens) and 3 to the right (ones), so 9 × 7 = 63. Read the left side first.

items.q: The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 6, fold down finger 6. What is 9 × 6?
items.e: Finger 6 is down. There are 5 fingers to the left (tens) and 4 to the right (ones), so 9 × 6 = 54. Read the left side first.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 9 × 8.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 8 = 80, then take away one 8: 80 − 8 = 72. Take away 8, not 1.

items.q: 10 × 5 = 50. Use it to find 9 × 5.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 5 = 50, then take away one 5: 50 − 5 = 45. Take away 5, not 1.

items.q: Which is a good way to work out 9 × 7?
items.e: 9 sevens is one seven less than 10 sevens: 70 − 7 = 63. Taking away 1 gives 69, which is wrong.

items.q: Which number is in the 9s?
4 × 7 = 28. Double it to find 8 × 7.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 7 is double 4 × 7: 28 + 28 = 56.

items.q: 4 × 9 = 36. Double it to find 8 × 9.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 9 is double 4 × 9: 36 + 36 = 72.
7 eights = 5 eights + 2 eights. 40 + 16 = 56. 54 is a common mix-up: 54 is 6 × 9.

items.q: Use the picture. What is 7 × 6?
items.e: The array is split into 5 × 6 = 30 and 2 × 6 = 12. 30 + 12 = 42.

items.q: Near fact: 7 × 7 = 49. Use it to find 7 × 8.
items.e: 7 × 8 is one more group of 7 than 7 × 7: 49 + 7 = 56. Add a whole 7, not 1.

items.q: Near fact: 6 × 6 = 36. Use it to find 6 × 7.
items.e: 6 × 7 is one more group of 6 than 6 × 6: 36 + 6 = 42. Add a whole 6, not 1.

items.q: Near fact: 8 × 8 = 64. Use it to find 8 × 7.
items.e: 8 × 7 is one group of 8 less than 8 × 8: 64 − 8 = 56. Take away a whole 8, not 1.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
Which is the same as 6 × 8?
items.e: 6 groups of 8 = 3 groups of 8 + 3 groups of 8: 24 + 24 = 48.

sets.title: Related division facts and fact families

items.q: These 32 dots are in 4 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
items.e: 32 dots in 4 equal rows: 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Check: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: These 18 dots are in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
items.e: 18 dots in 3 equal rows: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Check: 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: 7 × 9 = 63. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 7, 9 and 63 make a fact family. 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 ÷ 7 = 9 and 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 63.

items.q: 6 × 8 = 48. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 6, 8 and 48 make a fact family. 6 × 8 = 48, so 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Division starts with the biggest number, 48.

items.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 4, 6 and 24 make a fact family. 4 × 6 = 24, so 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Division starts with the biggest number, 24.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 8 × 9 = 72?
items.e: The fact family for 8, 9 and 72 is 8 × 9 = 72, 9 × 8 = 72, 72 ÷ 8 = 9 and 72 ÷ 9 = 8. 9 ÷ 72 is turned around: division starts with the biggest number.

items.q: Which is not in the same fact family as 4 × 8 = 32?
items.e: The fact family for 4, 8 and 32 is 4 × 8, 8 × 4, 32 ÷ 4 and 32 ÷ 8. 32 ÷ 2 = 16 is true, but it uses 2 and 16, so it is not in this family.

items.q: Which three numbers make a multiplication fact family?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4, 9 and 36 make a fact family. 4 + 9 = 13 and 5 + 7 = 12 are adding, and 4 × 8 = 32, not 36.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 54 ÷ 9?
items.e: 54 ÷ 9 asks: 9 times what makes 54? 9 × 6 = 54, so 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

items.q: Which multiplication fact checks 56 ÷ 8 = 7?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by: 7 × 8 = 56. Subtracting 8 once does not undo dividing by 8.

items.q: How many 7s make 63?
How many 6s make 36?
items.e: 36 ÷ 6 = ? Skip count by 6s to 36: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. That is 6 jumps.
Ask: 3 times what makes 21? 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Check: 3 × 7 = 21, so ? = 7.
Ask: 4 times what makes 32? 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Check: 4 × 8 = 32, so ? = 8.
Ask: 6 times what makes 48? 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 6 × 8 = 48, so ? = 8.
Ask: 7 times what makes 63? 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Check: 7 × 9 = 63, so ? = 9.
Ask: 8 times what makes 32? 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Check: 8 × 4 = 32, so ? = 4.
Ask: 9 times what makes 54? 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Check: 9 × 6 = 54, so ? = 6.
Ask: what times 7 makes 56? 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Check: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 8.
Ask: what times 9 makes 81? 81 ÷ 9 = 9. Check: 9 × 9 = 81, so ? = 9.
Ask: what times 6 makes 24? 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Check: 4 × 6 = 24, so ? = 4.
Ask: what times 7 makes 42? 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Check: 6 × 7 = 42, so ? = 6.
Ask: what times 9 makes 27? 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Check: 3 × 9 = 27, so ? = 3.
Ask: what times 8 makes 80? 80 ÷ 8 = 10. Check: 10 × 8 = 80, so ? = 10.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 7 × 6 = 42. Check: 42 ÷ 6 = 7.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 9 × 8 = 72. Check: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 6 × 4 = 24. Check: 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

items.q: This array has 27 dots in 3 rows. Fill in: 3 × ? = 27
items.e: There are 3 rows. Count the dots in one row, or think 27 ÷ 3 = 9. So ? = 9.
There are 5 rows. Count the dots in one row, or think 35 ÷ 5 = 7. So ? = 7.

sets.title: Word problems: canoes, hockey cards and the bake sale

items.q: Each canoe holds 3 campers. 7 canoes go out on the lake. How many campers is that?
items.e: 7 canoes of 3: 7 × 3 = 21. 10 is 7 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Muffins for the bake sale come in trays of 6. The class bakes 9 trays. How many muffins is that?
items.e: 9 trays of 6: 9 × 6 = 54. Use 10 × 6 = 60, then take away one 6. 15 is 9 + 6, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Benjamin has 7 toonies. A toonie is worth $2. How much money does he have?
items.e: 7 × $2 = $14. Double 7 is 14. $9 is 7 + 2, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, 8 students each raise $6. How much do they raise in all?
items.e: 8 × $6 = $48. 3 × 8 = 24, and double 24 is 48. $14 is 8 + 6, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: For the school concert, the gym has 9 rows of chairs with 8 chairs in each row. How many chairs is that?
28 students go on a field trip. Parents drive them, with 4 students in each car. How many cars do they need?
items.e: 28 ÷ 4 = ? Think 4 × ? = 28. 4 × 7 = 28, so they need 7 cars.

items.q: The hockey coach puts 42 pucks into buckets, 6 pucks in each bucket. How many buckets does the coach fill?
items.e: 42 ÷ 6 = ? 6 × 7 = 42, so the coach fills 7 buckets.

items.q: A sugar shack packs 48 bottles of maple syrup into boxes of 8. How many boxes does it fill?
items.e: 48 ÷ 8 = ? 8 × 6 = 48, so it fills 6 boxes.

items.q: Mateo reads 6 books this fall. Leah reads 4 times as many. How many books does Leah read?
items.e: 4 times as many as 6 means 4 × 6 = 24. 10 is 4 + 6, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 7 pairs of winter boots in the hallway. How many boots is that?
items.e: A pair is 2. 7 × 2 = 14. 9 is 7 + 2, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Priya puts 36 cookies onto 4 plates, with the same number on each plate. How many cookies go on each plate?
items.e: 36 ÷ 4 = ? 4 × 9 = 36, so 9 cookies go on each plate. 32 is 36 − 4, which subtracts instead of divides.

items.q: Hana buys 3 packs of hockey cards. Each pack has 8 cards. Then she gives 5 cards to a friend. How many cards does she have now?
items.e: First 3 × 8 = 24. Then 24 − 5 = 19. 24 forgets the 5 cards she gave away.

items.q: Juice boxes come in packs of 6. The teacher buys 5 packs. 27 students each take one. How many juice boxes are left?
items.e: First 5 × 6 = 30. Then 30 − 27 = 3. 30 forgets the juice boxes that were taken.

items.q: 7 flocks of Canada geese fly over the school. Each flock has 9 geese. How many geese is that?
items.e: 7 × 9 = 63. 10 × 7 = 70, then take away one 7: 70 − 7 = 63. 16 is 7 + 9, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Skates cost $4 to rent at the skating rink. 9 friends rent skates. How much do they pay in all?
items.e: 9 × $4 = $36. Double 9 is 18, and double 18 is 36. $13 is 9 + 4, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 63 chairs set up in 9 equal rows for the Remembrance Day assembly. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 63 ÷ 9 = ? 9 × 7 = 63, so there are 7 chairs in each row.

items.q: Lucas has 8 hockey cards. Aiden has 7 times as many. How many hockey cards does Aiden have?
items.e: 7 times as many as 8 means 7 × 8 = 56. Say 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8. 54 is a common mix-up, and 15 is 7 + 8.

items.q: Each pizza for the pizza lunch is cut into 8 slices. The class needs 40 slices. How many pizzas should they order?
items.e: 40 ÷ 8 = ? 8 × 5 = 40, so they should order 5 pizzas.

items.q: Each ringette team brings 10 players to the tournament. There are 4 teams. How many players is that?
items.e: 4 teams of 10: 4 × 10 = 40. 14 is 4 + 10, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Zoe plants a garden with 6 rows of tomato plants. There are 7 plants in each row. How many tomato plants is that?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42. 3 × 7 = 21, and double 21 is 42. 13 is 6 + 7, which adds instead of multiplies.
